# Commodity Supercycle Detector

## Purpose

Detect and track multi-decade commodity supercycles — prolonged, demand-driven upswings in commodity prices triggered by industrialization of a large economy. Supercycles are the most important structural force in commodity markets, lasting 15-25 years and generating enormous wealth transfers between producers and consumers.

## When to Use

- "Are we in a commodity supercycle?"
- "What phase of the supercycle?"
- "Commodity capex cycle analysis?"
- "Energy transition supercycle?"
- "Is the supercycle over?"

## Supercycle Anatomy

```
Phase 1: Demand Shock (5-8 years)
  Trigger: Major economy industrializes (US 1890s, Europe/Japan 1950s, China 2000s)
  → Commodity demand surges faster than supply can respond
  → Prices rise steadily, new investment initiated
  → Producer equities outperform

Phase 2: Supply Response (5-8 years)
  → New mines/mills/wells come online (5-10 year lead times)
  → Prices moderate from peak but remain above pre-cycle trend
  → Capex super-cycle: equipment, engineering, construction boom
  → Producer discipline begins to weaken

Phase 3: Overinvestment & Peak (3-5 years)
  → Too much supply comes online simultaneously
  → Demand growth moderates as industrialization matures
  → Prices crash, marginal producers fail
  → Capex collapse — 50-80% decline from peak

Phase 4: Purge & Bottom (5-10 years)
  → Industry consolidation, bankruptcies, nationalizations
  → Capex stays depressed — "never again" mentality
  → Supply growth stagnates as depletion outpaces new mine openings
  → Seeds of next supercycle sown in underinvestment
```

## Current Cycle Assessment (2020s)

### The "Energy Transition Supercycle" Thesis

**Bull Case (Supercycle Active):**
- Electrification = massive copper, nickel, lithium, cobalt demand
- Supply underinvestment: mining capex / GDP near multi-decade lows
- Mine development timelines: 10-15 years from discovery to production
- China+1 supply chain diversification = more metal-intensive infrastructure
- India early-stage industrialization = potential next leg

**Bear Case (Supercycle Over / Not Started):**
- China commodity intensity declining (property → services transition)
- Substitution and efficiency reducing metal intensity per unit of GDP
- Recycling rates increasing — urban mining reduces primary demand
- High prices cure high prices — demand destruction already visible
- Previous cycle's supply (commissioned 2015-2022) still ramping up

### Supercycle Scorecard

| Indicator | Weight | Bullish | Neutral | Bearish | Score |
|-----------|--------|---------|---------|---------|-------|
| Mining Capex / GDP | 25% | < 1.5% | 1.5-2.5% | > 2.5% | |
| China Commodity Intensity | 20% | Rising | Stable | Falling | |
| India/SE Asia Industrialization | 20% | Accelerating | Gradual | Stalling | |
| Global Manufacturing PMI Trend | 15% | > 52 rising | 48-52 | < 48 | |
| Inventory Levels (Aggregate) | 10% | < 5Y avg | Near avg | > 5Y avg | |
| Producer Discipline (M&A, capex guidance) | 10% | Disciplined | Mixed | Growth-focused | |

**Score > 70: Supercycle confirmed | 50-70: Forming | 30-50: Unclear | < 30: Not active**

## Red Flags
- Supercycles contain 30-50% drawdowns — don't confuse correction with cycle end
- China's commodity intensity is structurally declining as it shifts from investment to consumption
- The "this time is different" commodity thesis (electrification, energy transition) may already be priced
- Technology (AI-driven exploration, deep-sea mining, asteroid mining?) could disrupt supply constraints
- Demand projections by industry bodies (IEA, World Bank, mining companies) are systematically optimistic
